rebuildPipeline: A: node-pg-migrate up, every migration before seedBoundaryMigration
B: INSERT the tenant row, then seedTenantPolicy (Objects, Fields, Roles, Object CRED, Workflows)
C: node-pg-migrate up, the remaining migrations -> every MIGRATION_BACKED grant, stamped
D: apply GLOBAL CANONICAL_CATALOG grants (each cross-checked against the live Role catalog)
E: apply NONPROD_ACTIVATION grants -- environment-specific, never global

deployment.$comment: WHAT THIS FILE MEASURES, AFTER RULING E. It is the authority a DETERMINISTIC REBUILD of this repository produces -- the five-phase pipeline above -- and the rebuild guard proves expected == actual with ZERO unexplained. Ruling E requires a grant-bearing migration and the baseline that explains it to land in ONE change, so the moment migration 1762300800000 entered migrations/ this number moved with it. It is therefore AHEAD of the live nonprod row count until that migration is deployed, and saying so here is the point: 'what the repository produces' and 'what nonprod holds right now' are two questions and both stay answerable. This is NOT blessed live drift (AN2). Drift is a row in the database that nothing in the repository explains; this is a row in the repository that the database has not run yet, and it is named, counted and attributable to one migration.
deployment.appliedToNonprodBy: the ordinary deploy (functions migrate:up); lane BO did not and may not apply it
